observations.observation: NVIDIA’s September 27 presentation gave two distinct Anthropic figures: 2.6 GW contracted to date in NVIDIA AI infrastructure for shipment through 2028, and more than $180 billion in Anthropic reported contracted value across multiple cloud providers and neoclouds.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The presentation describes the $180 billion as Anthropic’s multi-provider reported value; it does not describe it as a single direct NVIDIA-Anthropic contract or as NVIDIA revenue. It does not identify Micron or allocate the memory-procurement commitments to any supplier.

observations.observation: Trade The News relayed the presentation’s Anthropic figures at 2026-09-28 11:43:49 UTC, the earliest timestamped third-party dissemination located in this search.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This establishes a timestamped relay before cutoff, not that no earlier public circulation occurred.

observations.observation: Before the roadshow, Bloomberg had reported separate large Anthropic compute agreements: $35 billion with NVIDIA-backed Lambda on September 1 and an $11.6 billion, seven-year Akamai agreement on September 24. This indicates that major compute contracting was already public; the roadshow added an aggregate figure and a distinct NVIDIA-infrastructure shipment figure. This comparison is an inference from the cited reports.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The earlier reports concern individual agreements and do not establish the composition, terms, or calculation of NVIDIA’s later aggregate figure.

observations.observation: The same NVIDIA presentation reported company commitments increasing from $119 billion to $279 billion, primarily related to memory procurement.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The presentation does not name memory suppliers or connect this figure to Micron.

gaps: The precise hour when NVIDIA’s roadshow presentation first appeared publicly is not stated; the investor-relations listing dates it September 27, and Trade The News provides a verified third-party timestamp on September 28.

No separate independent newsroom report of the $180 billion figure with a verifiable pre-cutoff publication time was established. Same-day coverage without a usable timestamp or dated pre-cutoff snapshot was not relied on.
The cited presentation does not break down the $180 billion aggregate, its payment or cancellation terms, or its provider-by-provider composition.
The sources do not establish a direct link from Anthropic’s agreements or NVIDIA’s memory procurement commitments to Micron orders, revenue, or supplier share.
research_notes: Cutoff: 2026-09-28T11:59:51.905006Z.
